name: Digital product interface
description: User-task, interface-use-quality, design-system, and visible-result governance for projects with a real product UI.

invariants.title: User task precedes styling
invariants.statement: A product surface is designed from its user, trigger, core object, result, and recovery path before colors, components, or decoration are selected.
preflight: Name the primary user task and observable success.
Mark the content, behavior, and surfaces that must remain protected.
evidence: Every major region and control has a task, information, state, action, trust, or recovery responsibility.
The primary task can be completed without relying on explanatory design notes.

invariants.title: Visual direction comes from project facts
invariants.statement: Visual direction is derived from project identity, real content, user task, target platform, and the existing design system rather than a generic style recipe.
preflight: Separate confirmed visual facts from open design decisions.
Choose the surface register and platform constraints before detailed styling.
evidence: The interface has a coherent hierarchy and recognizably belongs to the project.
Reference products inform relationships without silently expanding scope or copying unrelated appearance.

invariants.title: The interface contract covers the whole visible result
invariants.statement: Layout ownership, control topology, content and state families, responsive behavior, themes, input methods, and accessibility are decided as one interface contract.
preflight: Assign layout, boundary, scrolling, and overlay ownership.
Enumerate the reachable content, loading, success, failure, conflict, and recovery states that matter.
evidence: Controls expose the intended number of choices and the intended state transitions.
The primary task remains usable across the promised viewports, themes, zoom levels, and input methods.

invariants.title: Shared visual facts have one owner
invariants.statement: Semantic tokens, component states, and platform-shell adaptations have one active project design-system owner and explicit consumers.
preflight: Locate the source that owns each shared visual role.
Inventory every consumer affected by a shared change.
evidence: A shared change reaches all active consumers.
Superseded tokens, components, and local overrides no longer form a second visual truth.

invariants.title: Visible experience is verified through the real entry
invariants.statement: Interface completion starts from the formal entry, uses real content and state producers, crosses the actual runtime boundary, and ends in the visible, usable result.
preflight: Write the entry-to-visible-result chain before implementation.
Keep mocks outside the boundary the verification claims to prove.
evidence: The real application or site renders the result through its normal route.
Target states and viewports are inspected after the final relevant change.

invariants.title: Optional capabilities do not own the core task
invariants.statement: A capability described as optional or advanced does not gate the primary user's core object or first successful task; its state, controls, errors, and terminology appear only when the capability is available or intentionally being enabled.
preflight: Name the core task that must work without optional capabilities.
Define each capability's activation condition, added states, failure behavior, and interface location.
evidence: The primary task succeeds with the optional capability absent.
Capability-specific status and actions do not leak into the core interface while unavailable.
Enabling the capability adds its advanced path without replacing the core object's identity.

invariants.title: The interface feels coherent, fluent, comfortable, and fit for its task
invariants.statement: A visible interface is complete only when its spatial hierarchy, interaction path, feedback rhythm, platform behavior, and recovery fit the task frequency and risk as one continuous experience.
preflight: Translate the intended feel into observable decisions about directness, density, feedback, control, and platform fit.
Identify the natural task, repeated actions, input method, and error cost before polishing individual components.
evidence: The affected task can be completed without purposeless searching, backtracking, memorization, or mode switching.
Frequent low-risk actions stay direct while consequential actions slow down only where the user needs scope and consequence.
The real interface remains visually coherent, responsive, and under user control through waiting, repetition, failure, and recovery.

checks.message: Product surfaces must be governed from the primary user task.
The project must keep a complete interface and state contract.
Shared visual facts must have one project design-system owner.
Optional capabilities must not gate or rename the core user task.
The interface must be governed as one coherent, fluent, comfortable, and context-fit experience.
UI verification must reach the real entry and target viewports.

manual_verification.title: Primary task and visible experience
steps: Run the real product through its natural entry with representative content.
Complete the primary task and exercise its important waiting, failure, recovery, and repeated-use states.
Inspect hierarchy, design direction, control semantics, focus, and readability at the promised viewports, themes, zoom levels, and input methods.

manual_verification.title: Core task without advanced capabilities
steps: Remove or disable an optional capability without fabricating replacement state.
Complete the primary task and confirm capability-specific controls, status, and errors are absent.
Enable the capability when the product offers it and confirm the advanced path appears without changing the core object's identity.

manual_verification.title: Interface use quality through a continuous task
steps: Define the intended feel from the task, frequency, platform, input method, and error cost rather than from generic style adjectives.
Inspect the whole real surface, then complete the affected task from its natural entry with representative content and record searching, backtracking, attention shifts, feedback, and recovery.

Repeat frequent actions and exercise relevant waiting, failure, narrow-view, theme, zoom, and input states; confirm the interface remains coherent, fluent, comfortable, context-fit, and under user control.
